claim: Vantage/treasury-management capabilities are commercial-only; chapter has no SMB treasury-management product.
finding: Wells Fargo Business Banking markets 'Treasury Management Services' to small businesses, delivered through Wells Fargo Vantage and the Vantage app: wires (same-day or future-dated, approve/reject on smartphone), ACH payments (prepaid credit) for payroll/tax/vendor, Desktop Deposit (scanner RDC) and Vantage mobile deposit, ACH fraud filter pay/return decisions, dual custody, user transaction limits, ACH NOC/returns report. None of this is in the research dataset.
resolution: Add WF-P13-S08 'Treasury Management Services for Business Banking (via Vantage)' and add small_business to WF-P13.segments.

claim: Vantage is explicitly not for small business ('customers with personal and small business accounts... should download the Wells Fargo Mobile app'), so SMB gets no Tasks hub, Positive Pay decisions or payment-approval workflow.
finding: The App Store line steers personal/small-business account access to the consumer app, but the Business Banking site sells Treasury Management Services on Vantage to small businesses, including dual custody, wire approve/reject and ACH fraud-filter decisions. The conclusion that SMB gets no approval workflow is contradicted.
resolution: 'Small businesses use Wells Fargo Mobile/Business Online by default. Those that enroll in Treasury Management Services get Vantage, with dual custody, wire approve/reject and ACH fraud-filter decisions. The default SMB experience lacks a Tasks hub and approval workflow outside Direct Pay.'

claim: Small-business controls are uneven: Direct Pay has dual control, but Zelle, Business Bill Pay and Business Online wires can be executed by any single 'View and Transact' delegate.
finding: Supported for Business Online only, and as an absence-of-evidence inference: the OAA defines 'View and Transact' delegates and waives two-signature requirements, but no page states that dual approval is unavailable. SMBs on Vantage Treasury Management get dual custody for wires/ACH. Related step claims (WF-J17/REVIEW_AUTHORIZE/1, WF-J18/REVIEW_AUTHORIZE/1, WF-J03/REVIEW_AUTHORIZE/1) are tagged CONFIRMED_BANK.
resolution: 'Within Business Online, only Direct Pay documents dual control. Zelle, Business Bill Pay and wires can be executed by a single View and Transact delegate (INFERRED from OAA). SMBs on Vantage TM can require dual custody.' The related step-level 'no dual approval' assertions become INFERRED.

claim: Product inventory lists no official-check products.
finding: The online-services fee schedule lists Cashier's Checks orderable online (up to $2,000, delivered by mail, $10 + $8 delivery, $6,000 monthly limit) and Money Orders at branches ($5, up to $1,000), and online Stop Payment of checks/pre-authorized ACH ($30).
resolution: Add WF-P07-S03 'Cashier's checks (online order, up to $2,000, mailed) and money orders (branch, up to $1,000)', plus the online stop-payment MANAGE capability.

claim: Small-business payroll is covered only via Direct Pay.
finding: Business Online 'Transfer & Pay' lists 'Payroll solutions' (RUN Powered by ADP, third party) and Merchant Services (card acceptance with next-business-day funding) alongside Wires, Bill Pay, Direct Pay and Zelle. These are partner products, but the bank surfaces them in its money-movement menu.
resolution: Note in WF-P08.extra: Business Online Transfer & Pay also surfaces RUN Powered by ADP payroll (third party) and Merchant Services. Not modeled as WF products.

claim: Wallets listed: Paze, PayPal, Apple/Google/Samsung Pay.
finding: The bank also lists Garmin Pay among available digital wallets.
resolution: Add Garmin Pay to the WF-P11 wallet list.

claim: ExpressSend became available inside the Wells Fargo Mobile app (release notes 26.07.00, Jul 30, 2026).
finding: App Store version history first shows the ExpressSend note in 26.06.00 dated Jun 29, 2026. The dataset also keeps a later, corrected entry (obs:RC08), so the two conflict. research.md still says July 2026.
resolution: Remove obs:RC03. Keep the Jun 29, 2026 (v26.06.00) entry and the Sep 14, 2026 nationwide launch.

claim: Vantage mobile: domestic wire approvals (Apr/Jul 2025), Transfers create/edit/cancel (Jul 2025), Wires Status Search (Sep 2025), ACH Fraud Filter multi-item (Nov 2025), Tasks hub (Feb 2026).
finding: The iOS version history shows: Transfers experience 8.8.1 (Jul 1, 2025); ACH Fraud Filter multi-item 8.12.0 (Nov 12, 2025); Tasks hub 26.2.0 (Feb 17, 2026); domestic wire approvals 26.3.0 (Mar 17, 2026); Wires Status Search 26.9.0 (Sep 10, 2026). Two of the five dates are wrong. The Apr/Jul 2025 wire-approval dates could not be found on iOS.
resolution: Use the merged iOS timeline (WF-C009 resolution). Note that Android dates may differ.

claim: Vantage mobile 2026 (App Store dates)... supersedes the Apr 2025–Feb 2026 dating previously recorded.
finding: The gap-fill correction went too far. Several 2025 releases are real: mobile deposit PDF confirmations 8.8.0 (Jun 25, 2025), Transfers create/view/edit/cancel 8.8.1/8.8.2 (Jul 2025), credit-card accounts on home 8.11.0 (Oct 14, 2025), ACH Fraud Filter multi-item 8.12.0 (Nov 12, 2025). The 2026 items are correct.
resolution: Single entry: 'Vantage iOS: deposit PDF confirmations (Jun 2025); Transfers create/edit/cancel (Jul 2025); ACH Fraud Filter multi-item (Nov 2025); Tasks hub (Feb 2026); domestic wire approvals (Mar 2026); all wire approvals (Jul 2026); Positive Pay + Wires Status Search (Sep 2026); wire/tax/book/drawdown approvals + Cash Accounts (Oct 2026); home-screen payments tasks (Nov 2026).'

claim: Mobile approve/reject pending domestic wires (Apr/Jul 2025), tax payments, book transfers, drawdowns (Apr–Oct 2025 releases); 'Wires Status Search' (Sep 2025).
finding: These dates are a year early on iOS. Domestic wire approvals shipped Mar 17, 2026, all wire approvals Jul 21, 2026, and tax/book transfer/drawdown approvals Oct 13, 2026. Wires Status Search shipped Sep 10, 2026.
resolution: WF-P13-S02 / WF-J21: domestic wire approvals Mar 2026, all wire approvals Jul 2026, tax/book/drawdown approvals Oct 2026, Wires Status Search Sep 2026 (iOS App Store dates).

claim: Vantage (ex-CEO) mobile shipped payment approvals, Wires Status Search, ACH Fraud Filter multi-item decisions, a Tasks hub and RSA mobile token between Apr 2025 and Feb 2026 — fast cadence.
finding: Per the App Store history these shipped between Jul 2025 and Nov 2026. Payment approvals and Wires Status Search are 2026.
resolution: '...between Jul 2025 and Nov 2026 (monthly cadence)'

claim: Fargo is a differentiator: a gen-AI assistant that initiates Zelle payments (research.md: a capability no other top-4 bank markets).
finding: Bank of America markets the same capability for Erica. Wells Fargo's own pages call Fargo 'AI-powered' and do not say 'gen-AI'. What sets Fargo apart is its scale (more than 1B interactions; 3M Spanish-speaking users), not the capability itself.
resolution: 'Fargo (AI-powered assistant) can initiate Zelle sends and transfers. This is parity with peers (BofA Erica). WF differentiation is scale (>1B interactions; >3M Spanish-speaking users).'

claim: Only top-4 bank with a proprietary cross-border remittance product (ExpressSend) offering cash pickup in 12 countries.
finding: This rests on Wells Fargo's own claim ('the only major U.S. bank offering a dedicated mobile remittance service'). I found no independent peer check. Citi markets a proprietary 'Citi Global Transfer' service, so 'only proprietary cross-border product' is too broad. The cash-pickup uniqueness was not checked against peers.
resolution: Interim wording: 'Wells Fargo states it is "the only major U.S. bank offering a dedicated mobile remittance service"'. A peer check of Citi/JPM/BAC consumer remittance products (cash pickup, corridors) would settle it.

claim: capabilities.split = true
finding: 'Share costs, skip the awkwardness' is a marketing use case. No split-bill screen or multi-payer request is documented in the FAQ, the Addendum or the get-started steps. research.md itself says split is request-based.
resolution: split=false on WF-P01-S01/S02.

claim: states_shown: ['Accepted', 'Rejected']
finding: The public Instant Payments API reference gives the status vocabulary RECEIVED / PROCESSING / COMPLETED / REJECTED, with reason codes. The journey body uses this vocabulary, but the status_tracking block does not.
resolution: ['RECEIVED','PROCESSING','COMPLETED','REJECTED']

claim: ExpressSend states_shown: ['Sent', 'Available for pickup', 'Completed', 'Canceled'] (CONFIRMED_BANK)
finding: The mobile FAQ, mobile T&Cs, product page and press release mention only 'Activity' and real-time tracking. No status labels are published.
resolution: states_shown [] (labels unpublished), evidence INFERRED, where_visible 'Transfer Internationally > Activity'.

claim: Status vocabularies such as Processing/Sent, Paid, Pending approval, Approved, Processed, Invoiced, Open/Provisional credit are tagged CONFIRMED_BANK.
finding: Only Zelle (Completed/Pending/Scheduled), Digital Wires (7 statuses), transfers ('pending' after 8 pm PT), mobile deposit (processing/holds) and the Instant Payments API have published state labels. The other arrays are analyst reconstructions. J02 and J03 also copy 'Scheduled' and 'Failed' from J01, which do not apply to requests or receipts.
resolution: status_tracking.evidence = INFERRED for the listed journeys. J02/J03 states become [Pending, Completed].

claim: 'Insufficient funds => Transfer rejected' and 'Incoming payment returned => Sender notified' (CONFIRMED_BANK)
finding: Neither the Zelle FAQ nor the Addendum describes an NSF rejection or a return-to-sender notice. Addendum 10.G is a generic failure disclaimer, and the FAQ mentions email when a payment fails or is canceled.
resolution: Evidence INFERRED. The NSF path cites the FAQ failed-payment email.

claim: Bill Pay instant payments are sent over the RTP® network (The Clearing House).
finding: OAA §6(i) says the service 'may use' the RTP network 'or another third party network'. RTP is possible but not exclusive.
resolution: 'Instant payments sent via the RTP® network (or another third-party instant network per OAA §6(i))'. rail remains RTP.

claim: Bill Pay instant RfP payments are covered by the Bill Pay Payment Guarantee.
finding: The Guarantee page only carves instant RfP payments out of the deposit-account exclusion ('unless the transfer is an instant payment in response to a Request for Payment'). It also says instant payments cannot be stopped. There is no positive statement of coverage.
resolution: 'Not excluded from the Payment Guarantee (explicit RfP carve-out); no stop-payment protection'.

claim: RTP/FedNow credit posts in real time to Available Balance (CONFIRMED_BANK).
finding: The only bank evidence is the Early Pay Day exclusion footnote, which proves receipt, not posting behavior. Real-time posting is a network-rule inference.
resolution: WF-J15/EXECUTE_TRACK/1 evidence INFERRED.

claim: Network imposter-scam reimbursement policy (EWS, 2023) applies (CONFIRMED_BANK).
finding: Wells Fargo pages say only 'Qualifying imposters scams may be eligible for reimbursement'. They do not reference an Early Warning network policy.
resolution: Evidence THIRD_PARTY/INFERRED for the EWS link. The WF wording stays CONFIRMED_BANK.

claim: fees: 'None; stop payment $30'
finding: The $30 stop-payment fee in the online-services schedule applies to checks and pre-authorized ACH items. Bill Pay itself has no fee. Canceling a scheduled electronic Bill Pay payment carries no published fee.
resolution: 'Bill Pay: no fee; a $30 stop-payment fee may apply to stopping a mailed check.'

claim: Every published Digital Wires step references Wells Fargo Online, so the mobile wire flow is undocumented.
finding: The comparison chart lists Digital Wires enrollment as 'Online & mobile'. Mobile availability is therefore confirmed by the bank. Only the step-by-step mobile screens are unpublished.
resolution: 'Digital Wires is available online and in the app. Only web steps are published.'

claim: 'ExpressSend moved to mobile-only ... no branch/online path for new mobile enrollees' vs 'runs two parallel tracks'; research.md says app-only enrollment from July 2026.
finding: The bank says ExpressSend is 'moving' to mobile. The legacy branch/online FAQ is still live. Mobile T&C acceptance ends branch, web and phone access. ExpressSend Mobile itself is app-only. The two weaknesses should be merged, and the July date corrected (see WF-C007).
resolution: Use the merged wording in the WF-C025 proposed_correction.

claim: Recurring wires referenced in OAA §8(i).
finding: The provision is §8(h), 'Recurring and Future-Dated Orders'. §8(i) is Cancellation and Amendment.
resolution: notes: 'Recurring/future-dated wires (Preauthorized Orders) per OAA §8(h).'

claim: FedNow send participation could not be verified against the Federal Reserve participant list (XLSX unreachable).
finding: I parsed the live Fed XLSX (as of Nov 2, 2026). It lists 'WELLS FARGO BANK, NA, MINNEAPOLIS, MN'. The list has no send/receive flags (the RTN list is behind terms of use, which I did not accept). Combined with the bank's API routing to FEDNOW, fednow_send=true stands. Participation is now verified on the Fed list. the participation baseline participation (fednow_send 'unknown', push_to_card 'unknown') is stale relative to the research dataset.
resolution: Open question resolved. fednow_send=true with sources S912, S916, S952. Flag the participation baseline.

claim: sub_products_found: 37; research.md: 77 sources; research.md rail line: Push-to-card ✘ (no product found).
finding: the research dataset actually holds 40 sub-products and 112 sources, and rail_participation.push_to_card is true (Push to Card API, confirmed live). The research.md narrative is stale.
resolution: sub_products_found=42 after patch; research.md push-to-card ✔ (commercial).

claim: No evidence of dynamic scam interstitials or payment-purpose questions in the Zelle flow.
finding: A Jan 2026 press piece quotes Wells Fargo as saying it alerts customers to double-check the recipient. It is unclear whether that is an in-flow dynamic alert or static copy. Public bank pages show only static copy, recipient-name display and a first-time-recipient code.
resolution: Keep the weakness, qualified as 'not documented publicly'. An authenticated in-app Zelle send to a new recipient, or a WF statement describing the alert, would settle it.

claim: Access code text comes from short codes 93557/93733.
finding: Suspected error: the Zelle FAQ says Zelle texts come from 93557 or 93729.
resolution: Original claim stands: access codes come from 93557/93733. Zelle notifications come from 93557/93729 (already in CONFIRM_COMPLETE/1).

claim: Direct Pay is desktop-browser only (mobile not supported).
finding: Neither the current Direct Pay page nor the FAQ mentions a desktop restriction.
resolution: Original claim stands (CONFIRMED_BANK, S039).

claim: The first $400 of mobile deposits is generally available the same day.
finding: The Mobile Deposit FAQ gives only next-day availability for deposits before 9 pm PT and does not mention $400.
resolution: Original claim stands (CONFIRMED_BANK, S040).
